messages:
maria: FYI hitting a weird retry behavior in the Android sample when WorkManager releases network constraints — okhttp/retrofit seems to queue requests and then everything fires at once, causing token refresh storms and 429s.

aj: Ugh yeah that sounds like dispatcher + auth-refresh reentry. Are we using retryOnConnectionFailure=true in the client? That can mask connection flaps and cause bunching.

maria: client config in sample app:

```kotlin
val client = OkHttpClient.Builder()
  .retryOnConnectionFailure(true)
  .dispatcher(Dispatcher().apply { maxRequests = 64; maxRequestsPerHost = 5 })
  .build()
```

When WorkManager constraint lifts, all pending workers hit the network and our AuthInterceptor does a refresh per-call.

aj: Two quick fixes: (1) stop letting OkHttp auto-retry everything — do request-level retries with backoff, (2) make token refresh single-flight (mutex/synchronized) so only one refresh runs.

tim: Also note WorkManager backoff is only for failures; when constraint satisfied it launches queued workers ASAP. If jobs are enqueued separately you will get many concurrent uploads. We saw similar with image-sync.

sophia: Suggest marking uploads as unique periodic/one-off with ExistingWorkPolicy.KEEP so they don't pile, or have a single AggregatorWorker that drains a queue. Also consider setRequiredNetworkType(NetworkType.UNMETERED) for tests.

maria: Paste of the log spikes (snip):

```
2026-03-11 14:02:11.123 INFO UploadWorker: network available, starting upload (n=12)
2026-03-11 14:02:11.456 WARN AuthInterceptor: token expired, refreshing
2026-03-11 14:02:11.457 WARN AuthInterceptor: token expired, refreshing
2026-03-11 14:02:11.458 WARN AuthInterceptor: token expired, refreshing
2026-03-11 14:02:12.002 401 Retrofit: request failed (401)
2026-03-11 14:02:12.500 429 Retrofit: rate limited
```

maria: Each worker triggers refresh concurrently. We should avoid refresh-per-call.

aj: Sample auth interceptor pattern we use elsewhere:

```kotlin
private val tokenLock = Any()
var cachedToken: String? = null
override fun intercept(chain: Interceptor.Chain): Response {
  var token = cachedToken
  if (token == null || isExpired(token)) {
    synchronized(tokenLock) {
      if (cachedToken == null || isExpired(cachedToken!!)) {
        cachedToken = tokenProvider.refresh() // network call, blocking but single-flight
      }
      token = cachedToken
    }
  }
  val req = chain.request().newBuilder()
    .header("Authorization", "Bearer $token")
    .build()
  return chain.proceed(req)
}
```

aj: If you use coroutines, prefer a Mutex with withLock or tryLock to avoid blocking main threads. Also set retryOnConnectionFailure(false) and implement exponential backoff in the worker.

tim: One more gotcha — Retrofit call cancellation/coroutine adapter parity on Android 14 can cause requests to continue in OkHttp when worker is cancelled. Ensure worker cancellation calls call.cancel() and that CallAdapter propagates cancellation. We had a bug there.

sophia: Filed PR to sampleapp that (a) switches to single AggregatorWorker, (b) debounces token refresh with Mutex, (c) toggles retryOnConnectionFailure to false: https://github.com/redwood/sampleapp/pull/1234 :rocket:

ci-bot: build: PR 1234 — tests passed on emulator-pixel8, staging artifacts available (artifact://sampleapp/1234) :white_check_mark:

maria: Awesome. I'll try the PR on a Pixel 8 and an Airplane-mode toggle repro. If anyone can test flaky networks (mobile -> wifi switch) that'd be great. Posting a tiny repro branch: https://github.com/redwood/sampleapp/compare/repro-workmanager-retry

aj: I'll try on my Pixel and also add a small integration test around unique work + auth singleflight.

sophia: Heads-up: also saw duplicate 401s in older okhttp versions when Dispatcher queues were high — if this recurs we should log dispatcher.queuedCalls count before starting uploads.

maria: thanks all — moving this to a short PR to land the mutex + worker dedupe. Will ping when I have results. :ok_hand:
